memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"If you do this and God so commands, you will be able to stand the strain, and
all these people will go home satisfied." - Ex 18:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jethro ends his advice with four important words: "and God so commands."

He does not overreach. He has given his best thinking, and now he places it
under God's authority. He knows the difference between wise human counsel and
divine instruction, and he does not confuse the two.

That is a mark of trustworthy advice. Beware of anyone who presents their opinion
as though God has clearly spoken. And be careful of doing it yourself. "This is
what I think would be wise" is honest. "God told me you should do this" is a
much heavier claim.

Notice the two promised outcomes. Moses "will be able to stand the strain," and
"all these people will go home satisfied."

Both matter. Sustainable leadership is not only about protecting the leader. It
is about people actually being served. The queue that stood all day was not good
for anyone.

Notice also that Jethro does not promise the strain will disappear. Moses will be
able to stand it. There is still weight, but it becomes bearable.

That is often what God provides: not the removal of the load, but the strength
and structure to carry it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you distinguish between wise advice and God's clear word?
2. Are you asking God to remove a load He may want to help you carry
   differently?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me humility in the advice I give and discernment in the advice I
receive. Help me to stand the strain in Your strength. Amen.
